title_content.content: Read-through from INTC's 2Q26 and AMD Advancing AI 2026

paragraph_content.content: Key takeaways for the Asian PC/Server supply chain from Intel's 2Q26 earnings call (INTC US, covered by JPM analyst Harlan Sur) were: (1) better-than-expected 2Q Client sales, primarily driven by favorable product mix and price actions. (2) 2Q26 DCAI revenue upticks driven by strong demand across the board and supply improvement. (3) Sub-seasonal PC demand outlook and continued server momentum in 2H26. (4) Double-digit decline in PC demand in 2026. (5) Strong double-digit server CPU demand growth in 2026/27 and a sustained momentum into 2028. (6) Continued supply constraints across leading-edge logic, silicon wafer, memory, and substrate. The sub-seasonal 2H26 PC demand outlook echoes our cautious PC view due to memory price hikes. However, management sees incremental positive signs in server CPU demand over the next 2-3 years with strong double-digit growth. AMD (also covered by Harlan) has also raised its datacenter CPU TAM to US$220bn by 2030 from its previous estimate of US$120bn during the Advancing AI 2026, representing a 53% CAGR in 2025-30. This underpins our recent server CPU market research (Server: JPM proprietary server CPU shipment model). Overall, we reiterate our positive view on the traditional server supply chain, including ASPEED, Wiwynn, Lotes, and Unimicron. In the PC space, we remain cautious on key component price hikes and unit downside from negative price elasticity. We expect ASUSTek and Micro-Star to continue underperforming the index.
- Better-than-expected 2Q Client sales helped by ASP expansion; sub-seasonal 2H26 PC demand outlook: Intel's CCPG (Client Computing Group) revenue grew

QoQ in 2Q26, better than company and market expectations, due to cost-driven price actions and a favorable product mix. Looking ahead, management guided to a sub-seasonal Client revenue trend at flattish QoQ on softer end demand in 3Q26, which implies a likely sequential unit decline given continued mix improvement. This is largely in line with our expectations of a single-digit QoQ decline for NB ODM shipments in 3Q26. For the full year, management expects a low-double-digit decline in PC demand this year due to the negative price elasticity from memory price hikes and fading Win-10 commercial PC replacement demand.
- AI-driven general server demand strength: Intel's DCAI revenue increased

QoQ/YoY in 2Q26, driven by strong CSP/enterprise server demand and supply improvement. Intel's DCAI revenue is likely to see continued growth momentum in 3Q26 despite continued supply constraints (e.g., logic foundry, silicon wafer, memory, substrate). Management expects a likely stronger revenue uptick in 4Q26 due to better supply. This is largely in line with server ODM feedback of sustained server shipment growth momentum into 2H26. For the full year, Intel's management expects strong double-digit server CPU demand growth and sustained momentum into 2027/28. Strong server demand, coupled with content upgrades of new products, bode well for ASPEED and Lotes, in our view.

- Largely in-line PC/Server CPU roadmap: In PCs, 18A-based Panther Lake/Wildcat Lake (under Intel Core Series 3 line-up) are now in full-scale production for consumer/commercial PC market. In servers, Intel has launched its first 18A-based Clearwater Forest (i.e. Xeon 6+) server CPU. - 18A output above target; 14A ramp in 2028: Intel foundry revenue grew 6% QoQ in 2Q, with 18A output running 25% above internal targets and up 50%+ QoQ, per management. However, we believe this remains largely driven by internal Intel products, as external foundry revenue accounted for only ~5% of the segment in 2Q. Meanwhile, 14A is targeted for risk production in 2H27 and high-volume ramp in 2028—by which time, in our view, TSMC's N2 will already be running at high yields and approaching ~$80bn in annual revenue. We thus believe that TSMC will maintain 95+% market share in the front-end wafer market despite some small volume projects going to Intel given the extremely tight supply-demand situation.

- EMIB-T high volume ramp targeted in 2027: On advanced packaging, management noted strong interest in EMIB-T with a growing backlog, targeting high-volume ramp in 2027. Based on our checks, EMIB-T yields currently sit at ~60%. While multiple mainstream AI accelerator programs are evaluating EMIB-T given tight CoWoS supply, we expect most to start in small volume, with the largest project—TPU v9—reaching MP in late 2027-2028. Management also highlighted substrates, wafers, and memory as the most constrained parts of the supply chain. The company raised its 2026 capex guidance to >$20bn (with 2027 capex guidance to be significantly higher YoY), indicating an acceleration in cleanroom buildouts and locking in tool purchase orders. This reinforces our view that overall supply tightness will likely persist at least through 2027.
